questions.question: When was Subhas Chandra Bose born?
questions.answer_text: Subhas Chandra Bose was born on 23rd January 1897.

questions.question: Who was Subhas Chandra Bose's father?
questions.answer_text: Subhas Chandra Bose was born to Janaki Bose, a well-reputed advocate.

questions.question: Who was Subhas Chandra Bose's mother?
What was the profession of Janaki Bose, Netaji's father?
questions.answer_text: Janaki Bose was a well-reputed advocate.

questions.question: Where did Subhas Chandra Bose's nationalist temperament first come to light?
questions.answer_text: His nationalist temperament first came to light at Presidency College, Kolkata.

questions.question: In which city is the famous Presidency College located?
questions.answer_text: Presidency College is located in Kolkata.

questions.question: Why was Subhas Chandra Bose rusticated from Presidency College?

options.B: For refusing to attend morning assembly
options.C: For assaulting Professor Oaten over his anti-India comments
options.D: For giving an unauthorized political speech

questions.answer_text: He was rusticated for assaulting Professor Oaten for his anti-India comments.

questions.question: What does the term 'nationalist temperament' signify in young Subhas's character?

options.A: A desire to travel across many nations
options.B: A profound love for his motherland and resistance to foreign subjugation

questions.answer_text: Nationalist temperament signifies a deep love and patriotic dedication to one's nation and refusal to tolerate anti-India insults.

questions.question: What disciplinary action was taken by the colonial administration of Presidency College against Subhas?

options.A: He was awarded a silver medal
options.B: He was given a monetary fine
options.C: He was rusticated (expelled) from the college
options.D: He was transferred to another school immediately

questions.answer_text: He was rusticated from Presidency College following the confrontation with Professor Oaten.

questions.question: What fundamental moral quality did young Subhas exhibit during the Professor Oaten incident?

options.B: Uncompromising national self-respect and fearlessness in defending Indian dignity
options.C: Ambition to secure high government employment

questions.answer_text: He exhibited fearless national self-respect and courage by confronting anti-India slurs despite severe academic consequences.

questions.question: What do you understand about Subhas Chandra Bose's family from the beginning of the story?
questions.reference_answer: Subhas Chandra Bose was born on 23rd January 1897 to Janaki Bose, a well-reputed advocate, and Prabhavati Devi.

questions.question: Explain where Subhas Chandra Bose's patriotism first became evident and what happened at Presidency College.
questions.reference_answer: Subhas Chandra Bose's nationalist temperament first came to light at Presidency College in Kolkata, where he protested and confronted Professor Oaten for making anti-India comments.

questions.question: Why was Subhas Chandra Bose rusticated from Presidency College, and what does this incident reveal about him?
questions.reference_answer: Subhas Chandra Bose was rusticated from Presidency College, Kolkata, for assaulting Professor Oaten because of his anti-India comments. This reveals his fearless devotion to Indian dignity and refusal to accept colonial insults.

questions.question: Critically reflect on how Subhas Chandra Bose's early confrontation with Professor Oaten established his lifelong trajectory as a revolutionary leader.
questions.reference_answer: Netaji's early defiance at Presidency College demonstrated that he valued national dignity above personal academic career. Confronting Professor Oaten's colonial racism showed his uncompromising resolve to challenge British imperial authority, laying the foundation for his future revolutionary leadership.

sequence_test.description: These questions test whether the learner understands the chronological sequence of Netaji's early life and student rebellion.

questions.question: What happened first in the story?

options.A: Bose was rusticated from Presidency College.
options.B: Bose's nationalist temperament came to light.
options.C: Subhas Chandra Bose was born on 23rd January 1897.

questions.answer_text: The first event was the birth of Subhas Chandra Bose on 23rd January 1897.

questions.question: What occurred after Netaji's parentage was described?

options.A: He joined the Indian National Army immediately.
options.B: His nationalist temperament came to light at Presidency College in Kolkata.

questions.answer_text: After introducing his parents, the narrative highlights his student days and nationalist spirit at Presidency College.

questions.question: What prompted the disciplinary action resulting in Bose's rustication?

options.A: Assaulting Professor Oaten for derogatory anti-India comments
options.C: Moving to another city without permission

questions.answer_text: He confronted Professor Oaten after the professor made offensive anti-India comments, which led to his rustication.

questions.question: Which timeline represents the correct historical order of events?

options.A: Presidency College → Birth 1897 → Anti-India comments → Rustication
options.B: Birth on 23 Jan 1897 → Presidency College Kolkata → Confronting Professor Oaten → Rustication
options.C: Rustication → Birth 1897 → Anti-India comments → Parents introduced
options.D: Confronting Professor Oaten → Birth → Parents → Presidency College

questions.answer_text: The sequence starts with his birth in 1897, joining Presidency College, standing up against Professor Oaten, and subsequent rustication.

questions.question: How did the sequence of events at Presidency College influence young Subhas's political development?

options.A: It caused him to give up political ideals completely
options.B: It deepened his conviction that colonial subjugation must be actively and uncompromisingly resisted
options.C: It persuaded him to seek a quiet career in Europe
options.D: It had no lasting effect on his thinking

questions.answer_text: The rustication affirmed his uncompromising commitment to national freedom and established him as a courageous youth leader.
